title: Federal and government cloud editions: FedRAMP, DoD IL5 and other certifications as marketed

prose.text: {{fed-products}} Government host names and identity hosts are in [[shared.oneapi.government-clouds]]; the cloud names are in [[shared.cloud-architecture.cloud-names]].

Whether the government cloud has dedicated infrastructure apart from the commercial cloud is open {{gap:fed-dedicated}}. Whether new features reach it later is open {{gap:fed-features}}, and where its data is stored is open {{gap:fed-residency}}.

Federal adoption figures are open {{gap:fed-adoption}}. Whether the government editions are variants of each product is open {{gap:fed-editions}}. {{fed-names-zpa}} {{fed-names-zscalerten}} Whether zscalerten is a government cloud is open {{gap:fed-names}}. The innovations document the legacy doc cites is not captured {{gap:fed-govcloud-capture}}.

checks.do: For a question about certifications, answer as the page markets them and name the authorization level and product scope the page gives.

fed-zia-high.statement: The public-sector page says ZIA is currently the only secure access service edge (SASE) Trusted Internet Connections (TIC) 3.0 solution with FedRAMP High authorization.

quotes: Also, ZIA is currently the only secure access service edge (SASE) Trusted Internet Connections (TIC) 3.0 solution with FedRAMP High authorization.

fed-jab.statement: The page says ZIA and ZPA are both JAB-High authorized.

quotes: Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) are both JAB-High authorized.

fed-moderate.statement: The page says ZIA and ZPA have been FedRAMP Moderate authorized since 2018.

quotes: Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) have been FedRAMP Moderate authorized since 2018, allowing federal agencies, DoW commands, and federal contractors to take full advantage of the Zero Trust Exchange.

fed-il5.statement: The page says ZPA has achieved a Provisional Authorization (PA) at Impact Level 5 (IL5), as published in the DoW Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide, and that ZIA has achieved Authorization to Operate (ATO) at Impact Level 2 (IL2).

quotes: Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) has achieved a Provisional Authorization (PA) at Impact Level 5 (IL5), as published in the DoW Cloud Computing Security Requirements Guide.
Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) has achieved Authorization to Operate (ATO) at Impact Level 2 (IL2).

fed-certs.statement: The page's compliance section says Zscaler has achieved CMMC Level 2 certification, that ZIA Moderate Cloud has achieved GovRAMP Authorized status, and that Zscaler maintains compliance with CJIS, is compliant with FIPS 140-2, has achieved the ISO 27001 certificate and adheres to NIST 800-53.

quotes: Zscaler has achieved Level 2 certification under the U.S. Department of War’s (DoW) Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) framework.
Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) Moderate Cloud has achieved GovRAMP Authorized status, demonstrating our commitment to securing state and local government employees and data.
Zscaler maintains compliance with Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS), ensuring the protection of information as required by CJIS security policy.
Zscaler is compliant with Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-2, meeting NIST requirements for cryptographic modules.

Zscaler has achieved the ISO 27001 certificate, following the ISO/IEC 27002: 2013 best practice, attesting that our services are based on internationally recognized best practices for information security management and comprehensive security controls.

Zscaler adheres to National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication 800-53, ensuring sufficient protection of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information and information systems.

fed-products.statement: The page says the entire Zero Trust Exchange platform, including ZIA, ZPA and ZDX, is FedRAMP Moderate and High Authorized.

quotes: The entire Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform (including ZIA, ZPA, and ZDX) is FedRAMP Moderate and High Authorized.

fed-names-zpa.statement: The Terraform ZPA provider's documentation lists GOV and GOVUS in its supported ZPA cloud names.

quotes:
Currently the following cloud names are supported:
  * `PRODUCTION`
  * `BETA`
  * `GOV`
  * `GOVUS`

fed-names-zscalerten.statement: The Terraform ZTC provider's documentation lists zscalergov and zscalerten in its supported cloud names.

evidence.after: The following cloud environments are supported:

fed-govcloud-capture.title: The government cloud innovations document
fed-govcloud-capture.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Captures: zscaler-government-public-sector-marketing.md, zscaler-govcloud-innovations.md.' The legacy doc cites zscaler-govcloud-innovations.md, which is not captured under vendor/zscaler-help/, so statements that rest on it cannot be cited.

fed-dedicated.title: Whether government cloud infrastructure is dedicated
fed-dedicated.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'GovCloud has dedicated infrastructure separate from commercial — not just a logical partition.' No captured page says this.

fed-features.title: Whether features reach the government cloud later than commercial
fed-features.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Feature availability: newer features may launch in commercial cloud first, gov second; some commercial features are restricted in gov.' No captured page says this.

fed-residency.title: Where government cloud data is stored
fed-residency.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Data residency: gov-cloud data stays in-region (US).' No captured page says this.

fed-adoption.title: Federal adoption figures
fed-adoption.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Adoption: 1M+ federal users; 13 of 15 cabinet agencies.' The public-sector page's customer stories name the FCC and MCNC but give no such counts.

fed-editions.title: Whether government editions are variants of each product
fed-editions.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Regulated-cloud editions of the existing product line ... ZIA / ZPA / ZCC etc. all have gov-cloud variants ... not strictly separate products.' The public-sector page names ZIA, ZPA and ZDX as part of the FedRAMP-authorized platform (fed-products) and does not mention ZCC or editions.

fed-names.title: Government cloud names beyond the captured hosts
fed-names.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Federal Cloud variants (zscalergov, zscalerten, ZPA GOV / GOVUS).' The Terraform provider documentation lists ZPA GOV and GOVUS (fed-names-zpa) and zscalerten (fed-names-zscalerten) as cloud names, but no captured page says zscalerten is a government cloud, or that ZPA GOV and GOVUS are the federal variants.
